items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: I had a chance to join with Wendell -- he recommended me joining the Royal City Orchestra. Royal The Roll City Orchestra was a band that had been formed by a guy named Sterling Todd

ctx.x: Yeah, one boy. There was a boy named -- his name was Wendell Hayman. His father was a doctor. Wendell played the violin -- the violin. I'd go by Wendell's house. And Wendell (unintelligible) and the violin and my C melody saxophone. And Wendell would play. I'd play, and Wendell would say, "No, do it this way. This is the way it is." And Wendell taught me -- he really gave me my fundamentals, because he was a very fine musician. And then I had a chance to join with Wendell -- he recommended me joining the Royal City

Orchestra. Royal The Roll City Orchestra was a band that had been formed by a guy named Sterling Todd, who was a great piano player. And Sterling Todd had left Arkansas and gone to Chicago, you know what I mean, to further his professional, you know what I mean, career.

And so, we would have rehearsals. And I'd sit right next to Wendell, and as Wendell would play -- we would practice -- I'd go right over to his practically at (unintelligible) house practically every day. I'd practice with Wendell. And I got to be a good reader, see.
